title: Domain VI: Contract Development & Administration - Contract Development & Administration - Approval Process
subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: In public procurement, a program manager tells a vendor to begin delivering supplies before the contract is officially approved or signed by the procurement director. The program manager holds no legal right to bind the government. What type of authority is the program manager projecting?
options: Express Actual Authority
Implied Actual Authority
Apparent Authority
Sovereign Authority
questions.explain: Apparent authority occurs when a person acts as if they have authority to represent an organization, even though they do not have the actual, documented authority to do so.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: Because government entities are generally not bound by agents acting outside their actual designated authority, an agreement created by an unauthorized employee and a relying vendor is best described as:
options: A ratified agreement
An unauthorized commitment
An unconscionable contract
A tortious interference
questions.explain: An unauthorized commitment is an agreement that is not binding solely because the government representative who made it lacked the authority to enter into that agreement on behalf of the government.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: Which term describes the formal administrative process through which an agency retroactively reviews and formally approves an unauthorized commitment?
options: Ratification
Mitigation
Delegation
Subrogation
questions.explain: Ratification is the process used by a legally authorized official to retroactively approve an unauthorized commitment made by someone without actual authority.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: When routing a negotiated agreement for final signatures, which sequential strategy is typically considered a best practice to mitigate risk for the agency?
options: The Agency Head signs first, followed by Legal, followed by the Vendor.
The Vendor signs first, binding their offer, followed by internal Agency countersignatures.
Procurement signs first, followed by the Vendor, followed by Legal.
Simultaneous electronic execution is strictly required.
questions.explain: It is best practice for the vendor to sign first. This makes the vendor's proposal/contract a binding offer, which the agency then has the power to review internally and officially accept via the final authorized countersignature.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: What is the core purpose of 'encumbering' funds during the contract approval and award process?
options: To transfer money directly into the vendor's checking account prior to execution.
To commit or set aside specific budgeted funds to ensure they are exclusively available to pay the vendor.
To determine the appropriate accounting method for fixed asset depreciation.
To establish internal profit margins for the buying agency.
questions.explain: Encumbrance reserves part of an appropriation to ensure that funds are available when invoices matching the specific contract or purchase order are presented.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: A buyer executes an emergency contract using authority passed down via a formal written policy established by the Chief Procurement Officer. What type of authority does this buyer possess?
options: Apparent authority
Estoppel authority
Express actual authority
Implied authority
questions.explain: Express actual authority is explicitly granted to an agent by the principal, typically through written statutes, charters, or written delegations of authority.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: Prior to final execution, a multi-million-dollar technology contract must be reviewed by the agency's designated legal counsel. What is the primary focus of this specific step in the approval routing?
options: Ensuring the technical specifications align perfectly with operational needs.
Determining the vendor's long-term stock market viability.
Reviewing for legal sufficiency, format correctness, and statutory compliance.
Verifying that funds have been securely encumbered in the financial system.
questions.explain: Legal review prior to contract execution focuses on verifying legal sufficiency, ensuring all required clauses are present, limiting risk, and ensuring compliance with applicable statutory and regulatory laws.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: In accordance with federal regulations like the E-SIGN Act and corresponding state adoptions like UETA, what is the legal standing of electronically signed public contracts?
options: E-signatures are only valid internally and cannot legally bind a third-party vendor.
Wet ink signatures remain a statutory requirement for any contract exceeding the formal bid threshold.
An electronic signature carries the same legal weight and enforceability as a traditional wet ink signature.
E-signatures must be validated by a third-party escrow service to be considered enforceable.
questions.explain: Under the UETA (Uniform Electronic Transactions Act) and E-SIGN Act, electronic signatures are legally valid and enforceable in the same manner as physical ('wet') signatures, provided intent to sign is demonstrated.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: While an agent without signature authority cannot formally bind the agency, an agent with actual authority may sometimes bind the agency to commitments that are necessary to perform their stated duties. This legal principle is known as:
options: Implied Actual Authority
Eminent Domain
Non-delegable Duty
Apparent Authority
questions.explain: Implied actual authority is the authority to do whatever is reasonably necessary, usual, and proper to accomplish or perform an agent's express actual responsibilities.
questions.subject: Contract Development & Administration

questions.q: If a government end-user with apparent authority improperly instructs a vendor to change scope, leading the vendor to incur additional costs, why is the vendor at significant risk of bearing those unrecoverable costs?
options: Because apparent authority strictly allows for contract termination by the principal.
Because the government is generally protected by the doctrine of sovereign immunity against acts of apparent authority.
Because the Prompt Payment Act applies only to initial vendor invoices.
Because vendors are legally barred from seeking ratification.
questions.explain: In public procurement, unlike in the private sector, the government is rarely bound by the apparent authority of its employees. Vendors deal with the government at their own risk and must ascertain the actual authority of government agents.
